## Why a check is not automated, or is automated over less than it looks

| Check | Status | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `AC-1-bare` | deferred | project.is_bare is computed and never written: the column exists NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, two derivations produce the value, and create() hard-codes 0. Bareness is a property of a location and the column is on project, so whoever takes it must first rule on what a project with one bare and one non-bare copy reports. |
| `AC-8-live` | manual | No CI runner provides a WSL distro: nested virtualisation is not available on hosted Windows runners, so the in-distro worker cannot be started. Run on Reference A before a release. The bridge has never been crossed on a real machine here either — the dispatcher is asserted over a loopback worker only. |
| `AC-10-view-state` | deferred | No geometry restore exists: viewState always writes null for the window rectangle and nothing in the shell reads it. Whoever lands the restore must clamp to the measured top-bar floor in the same change, or a window narrowed once stays broken. |
| `AC-12-paints` | deferred | The e2e that renders the first-run screen skips itself when core/target/release/codotheca-core is absent — honestly, rather than passing over a blank window — so on any machine or CI job that has not built a release core the check does not run at all. Making it automated would mark a criterion covered by a test that silently declines to execute. |
| `AC-12-refusal-explained` | deferred | The shell distinguishes an unknown suggestion from an ambiguous one and the renderer collapses both to no root added: the commit path returns a root-add reply and the refusal type has no variant for it. What a user sees today is a scan that found nothing under a root nobody added. Closing it is a schema change plus 16b's surface. |
| `AC-13-no-second-core` | deferred | Plan 20's File Structure names app/e2e/acceptance_single_instance.spec.ts and no task in plan 20 or 20b creates it; the single-instance lock itself is the shell plan's code. Registering it automated against a spec nobody wrote would be a criterion marked covered by a test that does not exist. |
| `AC-13-focus` | manual | Focus transfer to an existing window is not observable under xvfb: there is no window manager, so focus semantics on a headless runner are unrepresentative of either target. |
| `AC-15-cold` | deferred | The terminal event now exists and has been observed: an end-to-end spec launches the real app and asserts a real pixel against a blank frame of the same window. Nothing times it. No harness records the pair below, no run has produced a p50 or a p95, and the spec that proves the paint skips itself when core/target/release/codotheca-core is absent. What is true today is that the app paints; what this budget claims is unmeasured. |
| `AC-20-resumable` | deferred | §4.1's chunking is unreachable today and accepted for phase 1: the git backend exposes atomic calls with no yield point, so there is nowhere to write a cursor. The contract is built — a partial outcome, its application and the cursor column all exist — so closing it is additive. Overturn on measurement, not taste. |
| `AC-20-duration` | unmeasurable | The criterion states no deadline — 'minutes, resumable, with a visible coverage indicator. No deadline.' There is nothing to gate on, and a ceiling invented here would gate on a number the spec deliberately declined to state. |
| `AC-20-large-history` | unmeasurable | The corpus tops out at the deep-history fixture, which reached 2,585 commits. About 30 ms fixed plus 0.02 ms per commit implies roughly 2 s at 100k commits and 20 s at 1M, but that is an extrapolation from a fit, not a measurement, and the harness records extrapolations as extrapolations. |
| `AC-21-cpu` | unmeasurable | Amendment 21 marks the CPU figure provisional: the 0.014 to 0.017% in the probe results was taken before any scheduled frame existed, so it describes a different build. It is re-measured before the public beta rather than gated on now. |
| `AC-21-audio` | manual | Asserting the app is absent from the OS audio mixer requires an OS audio mixer; no hosted CI runner exposes one, and a stubbed audio device would assert the stub. |
| `AC-22-database` | deferred | The file exists and holds the art half only. The other half was deliberately not stubbed, because a stub reports passed for a budget nothing measured, and the 1,000-project fixture belongs to the jobs plan and to no other. The file is shared; the owner is per-function. |
| `AC-22-gpu-residency` | unmeasurable | No GPU residency instrument exists in either language: App.tsx passes softwareCompositing to the tier hook as a literal false and tier.ts hard-wires contextLostThisSession, so both branches of the auto tier are unreachable (§27.7). The honest phase-3 deliverable is the instrument, not the compositor, and a deferred check with a budget would claim a plan is going to measure it. |
| `AC-23-audit` | deferred | The DOM convention the audit would read does not exist. No data-observed-at and no data-coverage attribute appears anywhere in the renderer today; the observation clause is composed in a formatter and rendered as text. An audit written against that convention now would select nothing on every possible tree and report clean — which is the same shape as the dead in-sync CI step. The convention has to land with the shelf first. The one clause that is gated today is the vocabulary: the destructive-token gate already fails the build on the word clean in a rendered string. |
| `AC-25-problem-location` | deferred | scan_problem has no location_id column. A project with two copies on two volumes can raise a problem on one of them and the row cannot say which, so the reachable-rows half of the criterion resolves to the project and not to the thing the user has to go and look at. The scan now writes problem rows, which makes the omission live rather than theoretical. Closing it is the schema plan's column plus the surfaces plan's rendering. |
| `AC-26-roundtrip` | deferred | Phase 1 ships no update channel. There is no auto-updater, no update server and no feed: distribution is a release page downloaded by hand. electron-updater is not a dependency and a gate asserts its absence, so the round trip has nothing to round-trip against. This is neither covered nor failing — the criterion's subject does not exist in this phase, and the check is here so that adding an updater later cannot arrive without it. |
| `AC-26-signature` | manual | The code-signing certificate is a hardware-token procurement and none has been obtained: phase 1 ships unsigned and the packager reports that posture rather than hiding it. The private key could not exist in CI even once it does, so no automated job can produce or verify a genuinely signed artifact. |
| `AC-27-appimage` | deferred | Phase 1 ships no update channel, so the AppImage self-update has nothing to update from. The AppImage target itself is built and packed. |
| `AC-27-packages` | deferred | There is no updater to disable and therefore no flag to carry. What ships instead is the stronger statement, gated today by scripts/check-no-updater.mjs in the bundle guard: the updater package is absent from the dependency tree and from the built shell entirely. That gate emits no joinable result row, so the criterion cannot claim it until either it does or this check is rewritten against what actually exists. |
| `AC-28-anonymise` | manual | A reviewer performs this before a release, against the built binary rather than the source. It is not automated here for two reasons. The cargo half (AC-28-fields, owner 17) asserts the document's shape but builds no bundle from host-shaped paths, so it cannot see an anonymiser that stopped covering a field. And the control half is what makes the result mean anything: without re-exporting the same index with real paths and watching the assertion fail, a clean run is indistinguishable from a run whose fixture never reached the anonymiser at all. That pairing is a judgement about whether the fixture was representative, which is why it is a person's gate and not a machine's. |
| `AC-29-linux-gpu` | external | Neither the maintainer nor CI can exercise it: development is on Windows with WSL, WSLg is unrepresentative, and CI runners are headless. Criteria 15 and 21 are measured on A and on WSLg only; the Linux figures come from external users during the public beta. This is a known, accepted gap and it is the reason phase 1 ships publicly as a beta. |
| `AC-50-readability` | manual | The criterion is marked half in the spec: whether condition, tier, rank and safety remain readable from static form alone is a human reading, and absence of a condition dot is a correct static reading rather than a failure. |
| `AC-50-reduced-motion` | manual | The override reaches the running window through the stored settings and the boot mirror, and every suite resolves the tier from injected inputs, so whether the packaged app honours the stored override is observed in the app, once per release, and recorded against the commit it ran. |
| `AC-51-voice` | manual | The spec marks this criterion as not automatable: no second-person accusation, no editorialised figure and nothing that congratulates volume are judgements about prose, and a machine reading them would be asserting a keyword list rather than the rule. |
| `AC-53-settings-shortcut` | manual | No suite drives the keystroke through the real window to the settings surface, so whether the binding works is shown only by pressing it in the running app, once per release, and recorded against the commit it ran. |
| `AC-56-effects-shell` | deferred | Split out of a single check that mixed runners. The notification clause has no shell module to assert against until the tray and the notice surfaces land, and the xp_events clause is a cargo assertion — registering all three together would have reported the criterion covered while a third of it was not. |
| `AC-57-windows` | deferred | The spawn-failure notice is shaped and reaches nothing: the failure facts are assignable to the renderer's notice type and no channel carries them across, and nothing stats the core binary for the mode the copy needs. The window cannot be asserted before it is delivered. |
| `AC-62-art-state` | deferred | Split out of the address check, which is a renderer assertion and cannot observe a database column. The two clauses were registered as one and only the renderer half exists. |
| `AC-65-chips` | deferred | The attention chip as built diverges from its owning section in seven values — padding, two gaps, border versus inset, three type sizes and a missing row border. Only the two declarations another section depends on were reconciled; the rest is untouched and unowned, so this check would fail today against the section it cites rather than against the component. |
| `AC-P2-20-13` | deferred | Documentation knowledge against a live API that neither the decision round nor this lane has called. It is honest as deferred and stops being honest the moment someone reads it as verified. |
| `AC-P2-21-3-floor` | deferred | §21.4 states the 60 s floor as documentation knowledge, and no call has been made against a live forge by the decision round or by this lane. The implementation carries the floor; whether 60 s is the right number is the part that is unverified. |
| `AC-P3-32-3-header` | deferred | Documentation knowledge against a live endpoint that no round here has called. AC-P3-32-3 proves the keying against a fake that names a resource, and a fake that returned the header would assert the fake. A response carrying no resource header is not mirrored and must not be given a synthetic key (§32.3), so its absence is a property of the endpoint that only an observation can establish. |
| `AC-P3-32-3-resource` | deferred | Documentation knowledge against a live API that no round here has called. The fallback is process-wide (core/src/sync/runner.rs:85) and its own doc comment calls it a guess that costs one request and corrects itself; whether the endpoint answers from core or from a pool shared with every other unauthenticated call the app makes is unobserved. |
| `AC-P3-32-16-caps` | deferred | Both caps are documentation knowledge with one datum behind them — one package-lock.json of 287,417 bytes (§32.6) — which refutes J6's 256 KB and says nothing about either ceiling. AC-P3-32-16 proves a file over the cap is not_read against a file built to exceed it; the values themselves are unobserved. |
| `AC-P4-38-6-win` | manual | The register is graded from Linux captures alone, and a clause naming both platforms is discharged on Windows only by a recorded Windows-native run of the core suite (R207), which no capture here carries. |
| `AC-P4-38-24` | manual | An audit, run against the tagged commit, that every producer this phase added has a production caller. It is a private release-checklist step whose tool is not part of the published tree, so no capture carries its result and it is recorded by hand (R199). |
| `AC-P4-39-5-win` | manual | The clause names Windows-native git, and every capture the register grades is a Linux run: a WSL run exercises Linux git, so the Windows half is recorded from a Windows-native run of the suite against the graded commit (R207). |
| `AC-P4-42-21` | manual | The clause holds on win32 alone and a Linux capture cannot discharge it (R207): the shell's vitest file is run Windows-natively and its pass recorded against the commit it ran on. |
| `AC-P4-42-25-nsis` | manual | Whether an OS notification appears is observed on a real desktop session from an installed packaged build; no runner here packages, installs and watches the notification surface, so a person records what that build showed (R200). |
| `AC-P4-42-25-portable` | manual | Whether an OS notification appears is observed on a real desktop session from the portable build; no runner here packages, launches and watches the notification surface, so a person records what that build showed (R200). |
| `AC-P4-42-25-appimage` | manual | Whether an OS notification appears is observed on a real Linux desktop session from the AppImage; no runner here packages, launches and watches a notification server, so a person records what that build showed (R200). |
| `AC-P4-42-25-linuxpkg` | manual | Whether an OS notification appears is observed on a real Linux desktop session from an installed system package; no runner here installs one and watches a notification server, so a person records what that build showed (R200). |
| `AC-P4-43-22` | manual | An audit, run against the tagged commit, that every producer this phase added has a production caller. It is a private checklist step whose tool is not in the repository and cannot run on CI, so its printed counts are recorded against the commit rather than captured. |
| `AC-P4-45-3` | manual | Reftable was measured on Windows git only, and the git the Linux capture runs cannot write a reftable fixture, so this criterion is graded from a recorded Windows-native run against the tagged commit (R207); a runtime skip counts as not run. |
| `AC-P4-45-12-win` | manual | The reftable clause needs a git that writes reftable, which the Linux capture's git does not, and the pseudoref behaviour was measured on Windows git only, so it is graded from a recorded Windows-native run against the tagged commit (R207). |
| `AC-P4-46-1-win` | manual | The round trip's Windows half executes the receipt's PowerShell block on NTFS. No capture the register reads comes from a Windows-native run, so the clause is discharged by a recorded Windows-native run of the same test (R207). |
| `AC-P4-46-13-win` | manual | SystemBinSettings reads the volume's recycle-bin settings from the Windows registry and bin; only a Windows-native run exercises that reader, and no capture the register reads comes from one (R207). |
| `AC-P4-46-14` | manual | Each case changes a volume's recycle-bin settings or policy and may raise a modal dialog from a windowless process, so it runs only on a disposable Windows virtual machine, never a developer's machine or CI; it is discharged by the recorded run (R200). |
| `AC-P4-47-5-win` | manual | The Windows-native git lists config keys the WSL and CI gits do not, and no capture this register reads runs Windows git, so the clause is discharged by a recorded Windows-native run (R207). |
| `AC-P4-47-6-win` | manual | Layer C must hold on Windows git over NTFS as well as on WSL, and no capture this register reads runs Windows-native, so the Windows half is a recorded Windows-native run (R207). |
| `AC-P4-47-7-win` | manual | The defect was measured on both platforms with different git versions deleting different refs, and no capture this register reads runs Windows git, so the Windows half is a recorded Windows-native run (R207). |
| `AC-P4-47-10-win` | manual | The group kill is a Job Object on Windows and a process group on Linux, two different mechanisms, and no capture this register reads runs Windows-native, so the Windows half is a recorded run (R207). |
| `AC-P4-47-11-win` | manual | Reftable was measured on Windows git only and the WSL gate's git cannot create a reftable repository, so this clause is discharged by a recorded Windows-native run (R207). |
| `AC-P4-47-14-win` | manual | The hook rule differs by platform, existence alone on Windows against existence and the executable bit on Unix, and no capture this register reads runs Windows-native, so the Windows half is a recorded run (R207). |
| `AC-P4-48-1-release` | manual | The version check runs as the release workflow's first step on the pushed tag itself, in a hosted run whose output no local capture reaches. It is recorded per tag with the version job's run id and the tagged commit (§49.6). |
| `AC-P4-48-2` | manual | The pipeline's first runs happen on the forge's hosted runners, against a pushed commit and then a pushed tag; no local capture can hold either run. Recorded with the run ids and the commit (§49.6). |
| `AC-P4-48-3` | manual | The launch job runs in the tag's hosted release run over the uploaded artifacts, which no local capture reaches. It is recorded per tag with the launch jobs' run id and the tagged commit (§49.6). |
| `AC-P4-48-3-hands` | manual | No hosted runner in the release workflow installs an rpm package, and while the floor step runs in report mode none runs a system at the glibc floor, so a person makes those launches on a real system and records the commit and what was seen (§48.9). |
| `AC-P4-48-6-capture` | manual | Only the packaged app, run on real Windows and Linux machines and observed at the network layer, shows every destination it actually reaches; a derivation from the source cannot. Recorded against the tagged commit (§48.4, §49.6). |
| `AC-P4-48-10` | manual | The floor step runs in the tag's hosted release run over the packed artifacts, which no local capture reaches. It is recorded per tag with the build job's run id and the tagged commit (§49.6). |
